source.source: PGDA LOLA 5 m/px DEM Site04 (Barker et al. 2021) + LOLA GDR LDEM_75S_120M (Smith et al. 2010)
source.notes: data/terrain.py: rays at 0.5 deg azimuth along great circles, 5 m steps to 12 km (PGDA where it has data), 60 m steps to 300 km (LOLA), exact sphere geometry (curvature included). Observer 2 m above ground 1737.2 m. DEMs are MOON_ME (DE421); the site lat/lon is taken as the same frame as Horizons (risk R3).

uncertainty.summary: Height error of the terrain that sets the horizon, divided by its distance: PGDA's own RMS error (toterr) in the near field; in the far field the RMS of LOLA 120 m minus PGDA 5 m heights where both exist (2.5 m, bias -0.4 m). Excludes features smaller than 120 m beyond the near field. Position-sensitive: the site is on Shackleton's rim crest. Moving it 150 m (the quoted precision of the IAU Moon rotation model vs the DEMs' MOON_ME frame) changes the horizon by up to 20 deg and the window's direct-to-Earth line of sight from 45.3% to as low as 27.2% (150 m west), at 0 deg mask. Checked 2026-11-14 in notebook 07_science_sanity_check.

source.notes: data/sites.py site_series('site04_shackleton_rim'), sun columns. Az/el are from the smooth local horizontal in the IAU Moon frame (Horizons). The terrain horizon in this file comes from DEMs in MOON_ME (DE421): the two lunar frames differ slightly, and the site lat/lon is taken as the same in both (risk R3).

uncertainty.summary: Apparent az/el (light-time and aberration corrected), not geometric, and no terrain (data/horizons.py observer_table shortcut). Horizons gives no formal az/el uncertainty, so the error here is unknown. angularRadiusDeg is one value at the mean Sun range (data/sites.py shortcut); the true radius varies over the window.
